where: PCS DESAT diode reverse sharing (New unclosed component-rating argument)
finding: PCS DESAT diode reverse sharing: preferred - 2 higher-voltage, low-capacitance fast diodes per channel; re-coordinate low-current Vf, blanking and surge behaviour; alternative - Qualify static/dynamic sharing network with existing diodes; no-change boundary - No-change only after bounding each diode voltage in every operating/fault state; a third diode alone is not proof
evidence: review R4 of 845131d; cost basis: 12 x diode premium (3W); 16 x premium (4W); no quote
recommendation: No blind waiver before full-voltage switching
closure: Verified and widened: the DESAT string sees the whole DC link on an off switch for long periods (normal 590-950 V; OV band 978-1048 V; 1071 V at the OV gates-off corner; latched after a trip 1094-1106 V, 1060-1061 V on a shared PV link, 1063-1130 V with the PV firmware dead; PV band top 1110 V) and with the gates off and the contactors open nothing fixes the split between the two switches of a leg, so the static envelope is 1130 V (design value 1150 V, the board checks fail above it); at 95 % sharing that put 1017-1074 V on one 1000 V US1MH, and no datasheet gives a minimum leakage to prove better sharing. Closed with option (A): 2 x Vishay BYG23T-M3/TR (1300 V, SMA, LCSC C145454, 0.1079 USD at 5,400) per channel on BOTH presets, each diode blocking the whole static envelope alone (x1.13-1.15), string 2600 V (meets the PCS rule 1.3 x 1445 V and the PV rule 1.5 x 1700 V); dynamic split <= 867 V per diode (C_J +/-20 % ASSUMED); C_J 9 pF at 4 V (not above the US1MH's 10 pF), trr <= 75 ns, I_R <= 50 uA at 125 C, avalanche 5 mJ non-repetitive; V_F at the 0.35-0.65 mA DESAT current extrapolated 0.59-0.81 V (ASSUMED, inside the existing 0.30-1.01 V band). PCS DESAT window 6.41-9.37 V unchanged (minimum 6.39 V, so the D-080 grade tables are identical), blanking 276-861 ns, hard short off after 1.26 us; PV preset 3 -> 2 diodes: window 6.41-9.37 V (was 5.43-8.47), on-state margin x2.0 (was x1.7), gen/pvcell.py asserts pass. Rejected: BYG10Y (standard recovery, trr 4 us), ST / FUXINSEMI STTH112A (dearer or failing SRC-2), SiC Schottky (capacitance at low voltage), balancing resistors (1.7 W per channel at the latched bus), a third diode (sharing unproven). Price: PCS-P125 +1.12 / +0.96, PCS-P125-4W +1.49 / +1.28, PV-P75 +1.84 / +1.59, PV-P100-110 +2.46 / +2.12 USD (catalogue / 5k). Open: the V_F extrapolation and tempco; a stored-charge mismatch after reverse conduction (bench: measure the per-diode split); creepage across one diode in layout (functional-insulation test route); no AEC-Q101 variant and LCSC stock 10,840 against 60-160 k a year; the DAB / GDRV-HB 1200 V class keeps 3 x US1MH (OPEN, x0.95 of its 1048 V peak) (D-081).

finding: PV/PCS battery-less bus: preferred - Prototype at 750 V and retain existing <=782 V coordination validity; model cable R/L and source extremes; alternative - Fast isolated intermodule inhibit for higher bus or mixed vendor interfaces; no-change boundary - Extra bus capacitance or brake/dump hardware only where energy cannot be curtailed promptly
evidence: review R4 of 845131d; cost basis: Firmware/harness contract first; alternatives require energy and quotation work
recommendation: No generic 909 V release from a lumped one-node model
closure: Model boundary closed: the coupled PCS / PV bus model now carries the inter-module cable as series R and L per PV module (ASSUMED harness: 2 / 10 / 20 m runs, 0.6 or 1.0 uH/m, 95 mm2 copper at 20 C) with the PV banks on their own node and the PV detection on its own port voltage, plus two source extremes (the PV study's slowest current loop 2279 Hz + 15.6 us computation; the coordination chain at its full x2 margin, 209 us later). The cable adds up to +28 V: at a 750 V set point the PCS node peaks 849 / 856 / 887 V (nominal / slow / slow + late), at 782 V 878 / 884 / 914 V - all ride through (soft limit 975 V); set-point validity with the cable 900 / 896 / 878 V (one PV module) and 884 / 878 / 846 V (two). Enforced product rule: default set point 750 V (three-wire and four-wire mode B; four-wire mode A needs 755 V: full-load floor 746.4 V + 1.7 V harness drop + 0.57 % PV measurement error), firmware clamp 782 V in the PV module's parameter set, the PCS refuses to start an island above 791 V on a bus declared battery-less (new firmware rows); the 909 / 921 / 846 V figures are model validities, not ratings (64 V margin from the clamp to the worst case). Harness contract for the integrator: <= 20 m per PV run, one run per module; <= 1 uH/m and <= 20 uH per run incl. fuses, disconnectors, busbars; DC+ / DC- routed together, no series chokes; loop resistance <= 12.6 mOhm per run (135 A, 1.7 V); nothing else on the link, <= 2 PV-P75 per PCS link, PV power within the PCS DC tier; as-built runs, the battery-less declaration, the set point and both serials in the commissioning record. Open: the harness figures, ESR / skin effect and the PV voltage loop not credited, unequal run lengths not studied; the bench confirms the peaks (D-081).

closure: Modelled with the PV method (ESTIMATES +/-50 %): with the fans off the inverter holds 20 / 15 / 8 kVA (three-wire) and 14 / 7 / 0 kVA (four-wire) at 600 V DC and -30 / -20 / -10 C inlet, 14 / 8 / 0 and 5 / 0 / 0 at 650 V, 3 / 0 / 0 at 700 V, standby only from 750 V (the L1 ripple loss, 148 W per phase at 950 V, exceeds what the closed enclosure sheds; enclosure = the PMA0125 body ASSUMED; the heatsink NTC limit 75 C binds).
